# rcaiman.registry

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

`rcaiman.registry` provides the infrastructure used by `rcaiman` to
describe imaging systems used in canopy photography.

Registry entries support hemispherical representation of observations,
including acquisitions that cover only part of the hemisphere.

The package implements a structured registry where instrument
characteristics and interpretation rules are declared through
specifications combined into registry entries. 

The package also provides tools to export and read **registry snapshots**
(YAML files) that capture a portable subset of a registry entry.

## Installation

You can install the development version of rcaiman.registry like so:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("GastonMauroDiaz/rcaiman.registry")
```

## Registry entries

A registry entry represents a complete technical description of an imaging
system. It typically combines:

- a `signature` declaring the expected metadata values
- a `band_spec` defining band interpretation
- a `geometry_spec` defining the directional reference frame of the image
- a `radiometry_spec` defining how pixel values should be interpreted


## How to create and navigate a registry entry

The package provides helper functions that allow you to build a valid
registry entry step by step:

```{r include=FALSE}
library(rcaiman.registry)
```


```{r example}
my_entry <- new_registry_entry(
  "Nikon_Coolpix5700.FCE9.CIEFAP",
  body = "E5700",
  body_manufacturer = "NIKON CORP",
  body_serial = "7053067",
  lens = "Zoom Nikkor ED 8.9-71.2mm 1:2.8-4.2",
  lens_manufacturer = "NIKON CORP",
  auxiliary_lens = "Fisheye Converter FC-E9 0.2x",
  auxiliary_lens_manufacturer = "NIKON CORP",
  institution = "CIEFAP"
)

path <- system.file("external/nikon_coolpix5700_fce9_ciefap_snippet.R",
                    package = "rcaiman.registry")
source(path)
head(metadata_rules, n = 2)

my_entry <- add_signature(
  my_entry,
  id = "raw",
  dim = c(1288, 962),
  validated_with_libraw = "0.21.1",
  validated_with_exiftool = "13.59",
  rules = metadata_rules
)

my_entry <- add_band_spec(
  my_entry,
  signature = "raw",
  id = "cygm",
  cfa_pattern =  matrix(c("Green", "Yellow",
                          "Magenta", "Cyan"), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 2),
  spectral_mapping = list(Red = "Magenta", Green = "Green", Blue = "Cyan")
)

my_entry <- add_geometry_spec(
  my_entry,
  band_spec = "cygm",
  signature = "raw",
  id = "simple_method",
  model = "radial_projection",
  parameters = c(0.63723886, 0.03455758, -0.02225094),
  center_of_vision = c(639, 469),
  normalization_radius = 377.6047,
  normalization_angle = 90,
  notes = "Documented in rcaiman.registry.data source code, folder data-raw",
  contact_information = "gastonmaurodiaz@gmail.com"
)

my_entry <- add_radiometry_spec(
  my_entry,
  signature = "raw",
  band_spec = "cygm",
  geometry_spec = "simple_method",
  id = "simple_method",
  model = "simple_polynomial",
  parameters = list("0" = list("Cyan" = c(0.0638 - 0.101))),
  notes = "Documented in 10.1016/j.agrformet.2024.110020" ,
  contact_information = "gastonmaurodiaz@gmail.com"
)
```

A registry entry available in memory can be quickly inspected to
understand which instrument it describes:

```{r print}
my_entry
```
`summary()` can be used to list the specification identifiers.

```{r summary}
summary(my_entry)
```
The `get_*()` helpers allow specifications to be retrieved easily for
use in scripts that interact with `rcaiman`.

```{r}
my_signature <- get_signature(my_entry, "raw")
my_bands <- get_band_spec(my_signature, "cygm")
my_geometry_spec <- get_geometry_spec(my_bands, "simple_method")
my_radiometry_spec <- get_radiometry_spec(my_geometry_spec, "simple_method")
```


A registry snapshot can be exported as a YAML file to be distributed
as metadata alongside preprocessed images.

```r
export_registry_snapshot(
  registry_entry = my_entry,
  signature = "raw",
  band_spec = "cygm",
  geometry_spec = "simple_method",
  radiometry_spec = "simple_method",
  file = "my_snapshot.yaml"
)
```

## On calibration

The functions `calibrate_geometry()`, `sample_radiometry()`, and
`calibrate_radiometry()` provide
support for implementing the simple calibration method described in:

Díaz, G. M., Lang, M., & Kaha, M. (2024).  
*Simple calibration of fisheye lenses for hemispherical photography of the forest canopy.*  
Agricultural and Forest Meteorology, 352, 110020.  
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.agrformet.2024.110020


## Registry architecture

The registry project can be organised as a small modular suite of
packages:

rcaiman.registry          → registry framework

rcaiman.registry.data     → registry entries maintained by the *rcaiman.registry* maintainer

rcaiman.registry.foo    → registry entries maintained by individual groups

## Extending the registry

The `rcaiman.registry.<foo>` naming convention improves discoverability
and signals that the package extends the registry project. Replacing
`<foo>` with a lab or project name provides an intuitive naming scheme.

Packages following this pattern would typically depend on
`rcaiman.registry` and contain `hs_registry_entry` objects
describing specific imaging systems. Alternatively, when resources for
creating a full R package are not available, a simple repository
containing YAML snapshot files may be deemed appropriate.

These extension packages are encouraged to distribute:

- the registry entry describing the imaging system and its specifications 
- raw image data
- the corresponding preprocessed output

Providing pairs of raw and preprocessed data enables testing,
validation, and reproducibility of registry entries.

GitHub repositories provide a convenient distribution channel for these
packages, particularly given the size limitations imposed by CRAN.
